```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(forcats)
```

```{r}
library(readr)
SleepStudy <- read_csv("SleepStudy.csv")
```

## {auto-animate=true}

::: {.fragment .fade-left}
An intro to ggstatsplot
:::

::: incremental
- Combines visualizations with statistical testing
- Can specify statistical approach:
  - Parametric
  - Nonparametric
  - Robust
  - Bayes
:::

## ggbetweenstats {transition="slide"}

::: incremental
- boxplot, violin plot, or mix of both
:::

```{.r code-line-numbers="1"}
ggbetweenstats(
  data = SleepStudy,
  x = LarkOwl,
  y = GPA
)
```

## ggbetweenstats {auto-animate=true}
```{r}

  data = SleepStudy,
  x = LarkOwl,
  y = GPA
)
```


## ggwithinstats {auto-animate=true}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-5|7"}
SleepStudy |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(WeekdayRise, WeekendRise),
    names_to = "Day",
    values_to = "RiseTime"
  ) |>
 ggwithinstats(
    x = Day,
    y = RiseTime,
    title = "Weekend vs. Weekday Rise Times",
    xlab = "Day",
    ylab = "Rise Time",
    pairwise.display = "significant",
    type = "parametric"
  )
```



## ggwithinstats {auto-animate=true}
```{r}

  )
```

## gghistostats
:::incremental
- Histogram automatically has median/mean line
- Using "grouped_" (similar to faceting)
:::

```{.r code-line-numbers="3|6|8-9"}
SleepStudy |>
  filter(AnxietyStatus != "moderate") |>
grouped_gghistostats(
  x = PoorSleepQuality,
  type = "n",
  grouping.var = AnxietyStatus,
  binwidth = 2,
 annotation.args = list(title = "Poor Sleep Quality for Different Anxiety Levels"),
 plotgrid.args = list(ncol = 1)
)
```

## ggscatterstats {transition="concave"}
:::incremental
- Creates scatterplot
- Shows histogram of each variable
:::

```{.r code-line-numbers="1"}
ggscatterstats(
  data = SleepStudy,
  x = WeekdaySleep,
  y = WeekdayRise,
  title = "College Student Weekday Sleep and Rise Time"
)
```

## ggscatterstats

```{r}
ggscatterstats(
  data = SleepStudy,
  x = WeekdaySleep,
  y = WeekdayRise,
  title = "College Student Weekday Sleep and Rise Time"
)
```

## ggbarstats
:::incremental
- Creates a Stacked Barchart
- Has visual percentages
:::

```{.r code-line-numbers="1|9"}
ggbarstats(
  data = SleepStudy,
  x = AnxietyStatus,
  y = DepressionStatus,
  type = "parametric",
  title = "Depression and Anxiety Levels",
  xlab = "Anxiety Level",
  legend.title = "Depression Level",
  results.subtitle = FALSE
)
```

## ggbarstats

```{r}
ggbarstats(
  data = SleepStudy,
  x = AnxietyStatus,
  y = DepressionStatus,
  type = "parametric",
  title = "Depression and Anxiety Levels",
  xlab = "Anxiety Level",
  legend.title = "Depression Level",
  results.subtitle = FALSE
)
```


## Strengths and Weaknesses {auto-animate=true}

Pro's

::: incremental
- Good for papers or work where viewer can spend time looking at graph
- Many of the arguments are similar to ggplot 
- Minimal inputs are needed to begin to use
- Very interesting and detailed statistics are easily available on models
:::

## Strengths and Weaknesses {auto-animate=true}
Con's

::: incremental
- Too busy visually for presentations
- Some naming conventions are different from ggplot (ex. grouping)
:::
